Q: What does Microsoft Defender Antivirus provide when turned on?
Option1: Real-time and scheduled antimalware protection

Q: Why are Defender definition updates important?
Option1: They add new threat signatures and engine updates
Option2: They disable User Account Control prompts
Option4: They convert local accounts to Microsoft accounts

Q: What is the main function of Windows Firewall on a workstation?
Option1: Filter inbound and outbound traffic based on rules

Q: When should you create a port rule in Windows Firewall?
Option1: To allow or block a specific port number such as Transmission Control Protocol 3389
Option2: To force apps to run as administrator
Option4: To add a new local user

Q: What is an application rule in Windows Firewall?
Option1: A rule that allows or blocks a specific executable regardless of port
Option2: A rule that changes the desktop wallpaper
Option3: A rule that disables sleep mode
Option4: A rule that forces password changes

Q: What is a local account in Windows?
Option1: An identity stored on the device and used only on that device
Option2: A cloud-based identity that syncs settings
Option3: An account created in a directory domain
Option4: A guest login that never requires a password

Q: What is a Microsoft account in Windows?
Option1: A cloud-backed user identity that can sign in to Windows and sync settings
Option3: An account that only exists on the local device
Option4: An account that always has administrator rights

Q: What is a standard user account best suited for?
Option1: Everyday tasks without system-wide changes
Option2: Installing drivers and changing system files

Q: What can an administrator account do that a standard account cannot?
Option1: Install system-wide software and change system settings

Q: What is a guest account in Windows?
Option1: A very limited local account intended for temporary access and usually disabled by default
Option2: An account with domain administrator rights
Option3: A cloud-only identity that syncs settings
Option4: A standard account for daily use

Q: What is the Power Users group in Windows?
Option1: A legacy local group with more rights than standard users but less than administrators, retained for compatibility
Option2: A group that controls power settings only

Q: What credential pair unlocks Windows by default?
Option1: Username and password

Q: How is a personal identification number sign-in different from a password in Windows?
Option1: It is tied to the specific device and user and used locally
Option2: It is always longer than a password
Option3: It replaces the need for encryption
Option4: It is stored on a remote server only

Q: What does fingerprint sign-in provide on Windows?
Option1: Biometric authentication using an enrolled fingerprint
Option3: A file backup to the cloud

Q: What does facial recognition sign-in provide on Windows?
Option1: Biometric authentication using a supported camera and face template

Q: What does single sign-on mean after the first successful logon?
Option1: Access to multiple resources without re-entering credentials until the session expires
Option3: No credentials are needed again until reboot
Option4: Passwords are disabled for all users

Q: What are New Technology File System permissions used for?
Option1: To grant or deny rights like read, write, modify, and execute on files and folders

Q: How do share permissions differ from New Technology File System permissions?
Option1: Share permissions control network access to a shared folder; New Technology File System permissions control access on the file system itself
Option2: Share permissions control only printers; New Technology File System controls only folders
Option3: Share permissions apply locally; New Technology File System applies remotely
Option4: They are identical in scope and effect

Q: What are file and folder attributes used for?
Option1: To set flags like read-only and hidden that affect behavior and visibility

Q: What is permission inheritance on folders?
Option1: Child items receive permissions from the parent unless inheritance is blocked
Option3: Only files inherit; folders never do

Q: What does Run as administrator do?
Option1: Launches a program with elevated privileges after consent
Option2: Prevents the program from accessing the network
Option3: Runs the program in compatibility mode

Q: What is the purpose of running a program as a standard user intentionally?
Option1: To limit privileges and reduce risk when elevation is not required
Option2: To speed up the program using more memory
Option3: To force the program to use a proxy

Q: What is User Account Control designed to do?
Option1: Prompt for consent or credentials before allowing elevation to administrator rights

Q: What does BitLocker protect?
Option1: Data at rest by encrypting entire drives

Q: When should you use BitLocker To Go?
Option1: When encrypting removable media such as Universal Serial Bus flash drives
Option2: When encrypting only one folder on a disk

Q: What is Encrypting File System used for?
Option1: Encrypting specific files or folders on New Technology File System volumes tied to a user certificate
Option2: Encrypting entire disks including the boot partition

Q: A user has New Technology File System Modify on a folder but the share permission is Read. What is the user's effective access over the network?
Option1: Read

Q: After installing a server app, clients cannot connect. What should you check first?
Option1: Windows Firewall inbound rules for the app or its listening port
Option3: Remote Desktop settings on the client

Q: You must protect only one confidential folder on a shared workstation. What should you use?
Option1: Encrypting File System on that folder

Q: A stolen laptop contained client data. Which feature best limits exposure?
Option1: BitLocker full-disk encryption with a recovery key
Option3: Setting a static Internet Protocol address
